title: Finite free continuous coefficient sheaves have invariant rank on a nonempty scheme
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ [def-pc-scheme], on its small pro-etale site [sk-def-pe-site] put $E_W=p_W^*\underline E$, where $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For $n\in\mathbf N$ let $E_W^{\oplus n}$ be the direct sum of $n$ copies of the regular $E_W$-module sheaf, with $E_W^{\oplus0}=0$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. If $|W|\ne\varnothing$ and $m,n\in\mathbf N$, an isomorphism $E_W^{\oplus m}\simeq E_W^{\oplus n}$ of $E_W$-module sheaves implies $m=n$. No quasi-compactness, connectedness, Noetherianity or invertibility of $\ell$ on $W$ is assumed.

proof.text: Give E the ultrametric instance IsUltrametricDist.of_normedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ]; Mathlib then infers that E is totally disconnected. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization] to obtain a monoid isomorphism φ from the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring to R(U)=C(|U|,E). These constructions retain the given norm and all universes.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6 (continuous-function realization on any scheme); elementary matrix evaluation and dimension comparison in the blueprint det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank proof, first paragraph

proof.text: For a regular R-module endomorphism h, apply the module action equation [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] after the lax monoidal inclusion of sheaves into presheaves. The ring-sheaf multiplication comparison [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], Sheaf.μ_comp_map_mul, identifies this with multiplication on sections. Evaluating on a⊗b gives h_U(ab)=a h_U(b), hence h_U(a)=a h_U(1). Therefore for any f,g, (fg)_U(a)=a g_U(1)f_U(1)=a f_U(1)g_U(1)=(gf)_U(a). Sectionwise extensionality proves that End(R) is commutative. Choose w in W. If its identity endomorphism were zero, evaluating it on the constant unit over the terminal site object and then at w would give 1=0 in E. Thus End(R) is a nontrivial commutative ring.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6 (continuous-function realization on any scheme); elementary matrix evaluation and dimension comparison in the blueprint det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along φ⁻¹ is additive. It takes the regular module to the regular module by Mod.regularIsoComapRegular and therefore takes each finite biproduct of r regular modules to the same biproduct of rank r by Mod.finiteFreeIsoComap. Conjugate the image of the given isomorphism by these comparisons to obtain R^m≅R^n. These comparisons include the empty biproduct.

source.place: Example 3.1, p. 6 (continuous-function realization on any scheme); elementary matrix evaluation and dimension comparison in the blueprint det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank proof, first paragraph

proof.text: A nontrivial commutative ring has invariant basis number, by Mathlib invariantBasisNumber_of_nontrivial_of_commRing. The singleton family consisting of the regular R-module is hom-orthogonal, since there are no distinct indices. Apply [lem-sfb-orthogonal-biproduct-multiplicity] to this family and the isomorphism R^m≅R^n. It gives an equivalence Fin m≃Fin n. Equality of their finite cardinalities gives m=n. In particular the proof covers m=0 or n=0.

Source check: HRS arXiv 2305.18131, Example 3.1, p. 6, says Λ_X = U ↦ Maps_cont(U,Λ) for any scheme X. Blueprint main-20261015 sk-lem-stratified-lattice-rank.proof.md, paragraph 1, says transition isomorphisms preserve rank because E_X(W)≠0. The item states exactly this comparison, with rank 0 included and no hypothesis weakened. Parent det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank steps 1–2 apply it on W = U_i×_X U_j, and the hypotheses match. Step 1: lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value makes |·|_E ultrametric, so balls are clopen and E is totally disconnected. lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization then gives an isomorphism of ring sheaves E_W ≅ C(|−|,E), and both inverse identities transport along it. That node is an accepted tool_use from unit sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors: it is only the coefficient bridge and is not supplied in this unit. The closure of the six proof_deps has 350 nodes and contains neither the item nor its parent, so there is no cycle. Step 2: the biproduct coordinates p_j i_k = δ and Σ i_j p_j = 1 are correct; adding module morphisms uses the module-morphism equation of sk-def-sfb-module-objects. Step 3: h_W(a) = a·h_W(1). I checked the indices (A is n×m, B is m×n); the (j,k) entry of gf at 1 is (BA)_jk, so BA = I_m and AB = I_n. Step 4: evaluation at w ∈ |W| is a ring homomorphism, so A(w) and B(w) are mutually inverse; no claim about field stalks is used. Step 5: the coordinate basis gives dim E^n = n, the images of the basis under A(w) are independent, and the card-le-dimension node gives m ≤ n and, by symmetry, n ≤ m. Edge cases: m=0<n forces I_n = 0, which is impossible; W = ∅ shows the nonemptiness hypothesis is necessary; non-qc, disconnected and nonreduced W need no extra hypotheses.
